Heckle

HEK-uhl · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To heckle to interrupt a speaker or performer with mocking or critical comments.

The comedian handled the hecklers in the front row with practiced ease.

Worked Example

A few fans in the crowd heckled the visiting pitcher every time he stepped up to throw.

Shouting mocking comments specifically at a performer or speaker, again and again, is exactly what heckle describes.

How Heckle Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

jeer

jeer: shout mocking or derisive remarks

Antonyms

cheer

cheer: shout in approval or encouragement

applaud

applaud: express approval by clapping

How Strong Is It? — interrupt → heckle → jeer

interrupt vs. heckle

interrupt vs. heckle: To interrupt is neutral; to heckle is to interrupt specifically with mocking or critical comments.

jeer vs. heckle

jeer vs. heckle: Jeer is close to heckle, though it can be even more openly hostile and less focused on a single speaker.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Heckle comes from an old word for a spiked comb used to separate flax fibers -- heckling someone is figuratively 'combing them over' roughly, in front of a crowd.

Use the root in a new word: hackle

Use the root in a new word: hackle: The related word hackle (as in 'raising your hackles') comes from the very same Old English root for a comb-like spike.
